title: The attentional switching framework: A dual process account of how the brain switches when attention switches
title_zh: 注意力切换框架：大脑在外部与内部注意力切换时的双重过程解释
abstract: The capacity to flexibly shift attention between external and internal events is critical for everyday tasks, yet research on how this shifting operates at the cognitive and neural level is still emerging. Here, we examined the question: How does the brain switch when attention switches between external and internal states? We propose the Attentional Switching Framework, which postulates that switching between external and internal attention states involves two seemingly opposing mechanisms subserved by distinct neural bases. First, based on our Resource Dependent Account, the regulation of attentional switching involves a domain-general mechanism that determines when and how the focus of attention shifts between external and internal states. This mainly recruits a similar set of brain regions and pathways when switching to either attention state, suggesting a common neural mechanism that initiates the attentional switch. Second, according to our Resource Independent Account, the maintenance of external and internal attention states involves domain-specific representations. These representations primarily recruit distinct brain regions and pathways, suggesting largely dissociable neural mechanisms that maintain the representation of each attention state. Together, we propose that when attention switches, the brain engages a dual process system involving a common mechanism that supports the regulation of switching and dissociable mechanisms that supports the representation of attention states. In highlighting the role of distinct operations of various brain regions and pathways underlying attentional switching, our framework reconciles apparent contradictions regarding whether common or distinct mechanisms are involved in switching between external and internal attention and presents important real-world applications and clinical implications.
abstract_zh: 灵活地在外部事件与内部事件之间切换注意力的能力对日常任务至关重要，但关于这一切换在认知和神经层面如何运作的研究仍在发展中。本文探讨了以下问题：当注意力在外部与内部状态之间切换时，大脑如何实现这一过程？我们提出了注意力切换框架（Attentional Switching Framework），该框架认为在外部与内部注意力状态之间的切换涉及两种看似相反的机制，并由不同的神经基础支撑。首先，基于我们的资源依赖账户（Resource Dependent Account），注意力切换的调节涉及一个领域通用机制，该机制决定何时以及如何将注意力焦点从外部状态转移到内部状态。该机制主要招募相似的一组大脑区域和通路，无论切换到哪种注意力状态，表明存在一个共同的神经机制来启动注意力切换。其次，依据我们的资源独立账户（Resource Independent Account），外部与内部注意力状态的维持涉及领域特定的表征。这些表征主要招募不同的大脑区域和通路，表明维持每种注意力状态的神经机制在很大程度上是可分离的。综上所述，我们认为当注意力切换时，大脑会调动一个双重过程系统：一个共同机制支持切换的调节，另一个可分离机制支持注意力状态的表征。在强调不同大脑区域和通路在注意力切换中所发挥的独特作用的同时，我们的框架调和了关于外部与内部注意力切换是否涉及共同或不同机制的表面矛盾，并提出了重要的现实应用和临床意义。
